checklist.step: Detect the reportable event and raise the EDI filing task
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Take the loss notice from the employer, broker or state hotline and open the claim in ClaimCenter with Line = Workers' Compensation.
Record Date of Injury (DN0031), Date Employer Had Knowledge (DN0038) and Date Claim Administrator Had Knowledge (DN0041) exactly as reported — these three dates start every statutory clock.
Set Jurisdiction (DN0005) from the state of the employee's exposure/employment, not the employer's headquarters state.
Confirm the claim triggers an EDI filing task in the 'FROI due' queue; if no task appears, raise a ticket to the Production Support Analyst before touching anything else.
checklist.done: the claim carries the three knowledge/injury dates, a jurisdiction code, and an open FROI task with a due date on it.

checklist.step: Confirm the jurisdiction's governing EDI release and clock
actions: Open the WC EDI jurisdiction table and read the row for the claim's jurisdiction: IAIABC release in force (R3.0 or R3.1), accepted transmission mode, and the FROI/SROI statutory day counts.
For Florida, confirm the FROI 00 clock is 14 days from the carrier's knowledge date and that the DWC is on Claims EDI Release 3.1.
Check the bulletin log for any state notice issued since the last table refresh that moved a clock or added a required element; if one exists, hand it to the Business Systems Analyst the same day.
Stamp the release version and the computed due date onto the claim's EDI task.
checklist.done: the EDI task shows the governing release version and a computed statutory due date derived from the knowledge date.

checklist.step: Select the FROI Maintenance Type Code
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Choose MTC 00 (Original) for the first report of a newly reported injury on a policy this carrier wrote.
Choose MTC AU (Acquired/Unallocated) or AQ where the claim arrived through a book transfer or TPA takeover rather than a first report.
Choose MTC 04 (Denial) where coverage or compensability is denied before any indemnity payment, and MTC 02 (Change) where a previously accepted FROI element changed.
Use MTC 01 (Cancel) only to retract a report filed on the wrong claim or wrong jurisdiction — never to fix a data error.
Write the chosen MTC and the one-line reason onto the claim note so the ack can be interpreted later.
checklist.done: the FROI carries a single MTC with a recorded justification consistent with the claim's compensability position.

checklist.step: Complete the jurisdiction's mandatory data elements
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Open the EDI data panel and work the Element Requirement Table for that jurisdiction and MTC, filling every element flagged M (mandatory) and MC (mandatory conditional).
Key the employee identifiers — SSN (DN0042), date of birth, gender, wage amount and wage period, employment status — from the DWC-1 / employer first report, not from memory.
Key Nature of Injury, Part of Body and Cause of Injury using the IAIABC code lists, and the Accident/Injury Description in free text (DN0037).
Key Claim Administrator Claim Number (DN0015), Claim Administrator FEIN (DN0187) and Insurer FEIN (DN0074) from the trading-partner profile, never typed by hand.
Ask the Policy Administration Analyst to confirm the policy number and effective dates as they were reported on proof of coverage, so the state can match the claim to a policy.
checklist.done: every M and MC element for the jurisdiction/MTC pair is populated and the policy identifiers match the filed proof-of-coverage record.

checklist.step: Run the pre-submission edit check and clear the errors
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Run the EDI validation job on the draft transaction and read the returned DN error list.
Fix data at source in the claim record — never in the outbound file — so the correction survives the next transaction.

Where an element is genuinely unavailable (e.g. employee refuses SSN), apply the jurisdiction's permitted default or exception value from the implementation guide and note the guide section relied on.
Re-run validation until zero errors remain, then mark the transaction 'ready to release'.
checklist.done: the draft transaction passes internal validation with zero DN errors and any defaulted element cites its guide section.

checklist.step: Release the FROI and start the acknowledgment clock
actions: Release the transaction from the outbound queue to the jurisdiction (or to the state's contracted EDI clearinghouse) over the registered SFTP/AS2 channel for that trading-partner ID.
Record transmission date and time, batch/interchange control number and sender ID against the claim's EDI history.
Compare the transmission date to the statutory due date and mark the filing on-time or late on the spot — a late filing is logged now, not at month end.
Set the acknowledgment watch to 5 business days; anything unacknowledged past that goes to the reject/aging process.
checklist.done: the FROI is transmitted with a recorded control number and timestamp, flagged on-time or late, and an ack watch is running.

checklist.step: File SROI IP when the first indemnity payment issues
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: On issuing the first indemnity payment, take the payment date, Benefit Type Code (e.g. 050 temporary total), Benefit Period Start/Through dates, Benefit Amount Paid and Average Weekly Wage from the payment transaction.
Raise SROI MTC IP (Initial Payment), or EP where the employer paid the first benefit, or AP on an acquired claim.
Populate the Benefit and Payment segments and the paid-to-date buckets (indemnity, medical, expense) from the claim financials — not from a manual tally.
Release the SROI inside the jurisdiction clock (Florida: 14 days from the first indemnity payment) and record the transmission against the claim.
checklist.done: the SROI IP is transmitted within the jurisdiction clock with benefit type, period, amount and AWW tied to the actual payment transaction.

checklist.step: File SROI on benefit changes, suspensions and reinstatements
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Raise SROI CA/CB when the benefit type or the weekly amount changes, carrying the new Benefit Type Code and effective date.
Raise SROI SA/SB on suspension and select the correct suspension reason code (return to work, medical release, claimant non-cooperation, benefits exhausted, death).
Raise SROI RB on reinstatement with the reinstatement date and the resumed benefit type.
Confirm the maximum/minimum compensation rate applied matches the jurisdiction's rate table for the year of injury before releasing.
Give the Medical / Nurse Case Manager notice of any suspension driven by a medical release so the file narrative and the EDI record agree.
checklist.done: every benefit change, suspension and reinstatement has a matching SROI with the correct code and effective date inside the state clock.

checklist.step: File the denial transaction when compensability or coverage is declined
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Record the denial decision date and the denial reason code (no coverage, not in course and scope, late notice, idiopathic, statute of limitations) on the claim.
Raise FROI 04 where no FROI has yet been accepted, or SROI 04 where the claim is already on file with the state.
Attach the denial letter issued to the employee and employer to the claim file and confirm the mail date is on or before the EDI transmission date.
Release the denial transaction within the Florida 14-day denial clock (or the sampled jurisdiction's equivalent) and diary the state's dispute window.
checklist.done: the denial transaction is transmitted within the jurisdiction's denial clock and matches the dated denial letter on the claim file.

checklist.step: Capture the acknowledgment and reconcile it to the transmission
actions: Pull the day's inbound acknowledgment files from the jurisdiction mailbox and load them against the outbound control numbers.
Read the application acknowledgment code per transaction: TA (accepted), TE (accepted with errors) or TR (rejected), plus any DN error numbers and error message codes.
Write the jurisdiction claim number returned on an accepted FROI back onto the claim — later SROIs will be rejected without it.
Reconcile counts: transactions released today versus acknowledgments received; list anything unmatched for the reject/aging process.
checklist.done: every released transaction has a matched acknowledgment with its code recorded, or sits on the unmatched list with an owner.

checklist.step: Correct and resubmit TE and TR transactions inside the state's correction window
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Open each TE/TR item, translate the DN error number against the jurisdiction's error message table, and identify the failing element.
Correct the underlying claim data and re-release: a TR transaction is not on file at all, so the original MTC is re-sent, while a TE is fixed by an MTC 02 change transaction.
Track the correction against the state's correction window and, where the original clock has already run, treat the filing as late and log it.
Hand any error appearing on three or more claims in a week to the Business Systems Analyst as a suspected mapping or edit-table defect.
checklist.done: every TE/TR is corrected and re-acknowledged as accepted, with recurring error patterns handed to IT.

checklist.step: File the periodic and final SROI reports the jurisdiction demands
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Work the diary for SROI PY (payment report) and SROI AN (annual report) where the jurisdiction requires periodic paid-to-date reporting on open claims.
On final payment, raise SROI FN with the final paid-to-date indemnity, medical and expense figures and the claim closure date.
Reconcile the paid-to-date figures on the SROI to the claim payment ledger before release — a mismatch here reappears in the unit-statistical report.
Confirm any settlement or lump-sum award is reported with the correct benefit type and award date.
checklist.done: periodic and final SROI reports are filed on diary with paid-to-date figures that tie to the claim payment ledger.

checklist.step: Work the daily timeliness dashboard and escalate slipping clocks
actions: Open the WC EDI timeliness dashboard each morning and read three tiles: FROI due in 3 days, FROI past due, SROI IP past due — each split by jurisdiction.
Reassign any past-due item to a named adjuster with a same-day filing instruction.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance any jurisdiction showing more than two past-due FROIs in a rolling week.
Record the daily review as a dated dashboard export so the control has evidence of operation.
checklist.done: the dashboard is reviewed and exported daily, with every past-due item reassigned and named-jurisdiction breaches escalated.

checklist.step: Log late or missed filings and prepare the regulator position
actions: Raise an issue per late or missed filing with claim number, jurisdiction, MTC, statutory due date, actual transmission date and the day count over.
Assign a root cause (late employer report, wrong jurisdiction coded, missing policy match, translator outage, adjuster backlog) and an owner.
Where a Florida DWC penalty notice arrives, assemble the transmission history and route the response through Regulatory Counsel before filing it.
Carry every open issue into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
checklist.done: every late or missed filing has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

checklist.step: Retain the transmission and acknowledgment evidence on the claim file
actions: Archive the outbound transaction image, the acknowledgment with its code and DN errors, and the full resubmission chain against the claim in the document repository.
Apply the retention label 'life of claim + 5 years' so the record survives claim closure.
Index each record by jurisdiction, claim administrator claim number, jurisdiction claim number and transmission date so an examiner request can be answered by any of them.
Spot-check ten archived claims a month to confirm the images are readable and the index returns them.
checklist.done: transmission and acknowledgment evidence is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by jurisdiction claim number.

testing.step: Build the population of reportable events for the month
actions: Extract from the claims event log every WC claim in the 30 EDI jurisdictions with a first-knowledge date, first indemnity payment, benefit change, suspension, reinstatement, denial or final payment dated in the month.
Add medical-only claims for jurisdictions that require FROI on medical-only, so a filing category cannot fall out of scope.
Record population counts by jurisdiction and event type and sign the extract as complete with the extraction query and run date.
testing.done: the population is extracted by jurisdiction and event type, counted, and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the claim payment ledger and the intake register
actions: Reconcile first-indemnity-payment events to the payment ledger's first indemnity disbursement per claim for the month and explain every difference.
Reconcile new-claim counts to the intake register (loss notices received) so claims opened but never event-flagged are exposed.
Confirm the jurisdiction on each claim against the employee's state of employment recorded on the claim, not the employer's mailing state.
List any claim present in the ledger or register but absent from the event population as an automatic exception.
testing.done: population, payment ledger and intake register agree, with every difference explained or raised as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Florida lost-time claims and 100% of claims in any jurisdiction that issued a penalty notice in the last 12 months.
Take 40 further events selected at random with a recorded seed, stratified so each event type (FROI 00, FROI 04, SROI IP, SROI SA, SROI FN) appears at least five times.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, stratified across event types and covers Florida lost-time in full.

testing.step: Re-perform the MTC selection on each sampled event
testing.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Read the claim narrative, compensability decision and payment history and reach your own MTC conclusion before opening the EDI history.
Compare to the MTC actually transmitted; a denial reported as an MTC 02 change, or a benefit change reported as an IP, is an exception.
Check MTC 01 (Cancel) was not used to patch a data error rather than to retract a wrongly-filed report.
Record the independent conclusion, the transmitted MTC and the difference on the workpaper line.
testing.done: each sampled event carries an independent MTC conclusion and any disagreement with the transmitted MTC is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform data element accuracy against the source documents
actions: For each sampled transaction, compare Date of Injury, employer knowledge date, wage amount and period, Nature/Part/Cause of Injury and employment status back to the employer's first report and the wage statement in the claim file.
Compare Insurer FEIN, Claim Administrator FEIN and policy number to the trading-partner profile and to the filed proof-of-coverage record for that policy.
Confirm every element the jurisdiction's Element Requirement Table marks M or MC for that MTC was actually populated.
Treat a populated-but-wrong element the same as a missing one — the state matched a claim to the wrong policy either way.
testing.done: each sampled transaction's mandatory elements are traced to source documents with differences listed element by element.

testing.step: Trace each sampled transmission to an accepted acknowledgment
actions: Search the EDI history by batch/interchange control number and confirm an acknowledgment exists for the sampled transaction.
Read the final disposition: TA, TE with DN errors, or TR, and confirm any TE/TR was followed by a re-transmission that reached TA.
Confirm the jurisdiction claim number returned on the accepted FROI was written back onto the claim record.
Capture the acknowledgment detail screen into the workpaper as the trace evidence.
testing.done: every sampled transaction traces to a final accepted acknowledgment with the jurisdiction claim number recorded.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory day counts
actions: For each sampled FROI recompute elapsed days = transmission date − claim administrator knowledge date and compare to the jurisdiction clock (Florida 14 days).
For each sampled SROI IP recompute elapsed days = transmission date − first indemnity payment date against the same clock.

Apply the jurisdiction's own convention on calendar versus business days and on whether the clock runs from employer or carrier knowledge — a wrong convention understates lateness across the whole file.
Recompute the reported timeliness percentage from the sample and compare it to the operational dashboard figure for the month.
testing.done: day counts are independently recomputed, the clock convention is confirmed per jurisdiction, and the recomputed timeliness rate is reconciled to the dashboard.

testing.step: Test closure of rejected transactions inside the correction window
actions: Extract all TR and TE acknowledgments for the month and age each one from acknowledgment date to accepted re-transmission date.
Compare that age to the jurisdiction's correction window and list anything still open or corrected late.
Confirm the correction was applied to the claim record at source, by re-reading the element on the claim rather than in the outbound file.
Confirm no transaction was closed administratively without an accepted acknowledgment.
testing.done: every rejected transaction is shown corrected and re-accepted within the correction window, or listed as an open exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying claim number, jurisdiction, MTC, event date, statutory due date, actual transmission date and days over.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (late employer report, wrong jurisdiction, missing policy match, translator outage, adjuster backlog, edit-table defect) and a named owner.
Quantify penalty exposure per jurisdiction and flag any claim where a missed FROI may have delayed a benefit to the injured worker.
Open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any wholly unfiled reportable event.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a quantified penalty exposure.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute FROI and SROI timeliness rates from the sample and compare to the 99%/98% thresholds and the zero-unfiled rule.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing the workpaper references behind each exception.
Have the independent reviewer, who keyed or released none of the sampled transactions, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any open unfiled events to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with timeliness rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Inventory every jurisdiction the book requires EDI reporting in
actions: Pull the list of states where WC policies are in force from the policy administration in-force extract and compare it to the 30 registered EDI jurisdictions.
For each state, record the reporting programme in force: claims EDI (FROI/SROI), proof of coverage, and medical bill EDI where mandated.
Flag any state with in-force premium but no registration as an immediate gap and raise it to the Head of IT the same day.
Publish the jurisdiction inventory with an as-at date into the regulatory register.
checklist.done: the jurisdiction inventory reconciles state-by-state to the in-force policy extract with no unregistered writing state.

checklist.step: Obtain and complete each state's trading-partner profile and agreement
actions: Download the current trading-partner profile and trading-partner agreement forms from the state WC division's EDI page — for Alabama, the WC Division's EDI trading-partner packet.
Complete the insurer and claim administrator legal names, FEINs, NAIC company codes, sender ID, postal code and the named EDI technical and business contacts with direct phone and email.
Declare the IAIABC release and transaction sets being sent (Claims R3.1 FROI/SROI) and the transmission mode requested.
Route the agreement for authorised officer signature, then file the signed original in the document repository under WC-EDI/<state>/registration.
checklist.done: a signed, current profile and agreement exist for the state with named contacts, FEINs, sender ID and declared transaction sets.

checklist.step: Register the sender identifiers and reconcile them to the claim systems
actions: Enter the state-assigned trading-partner ID, sender ID and receiver ID into the EDI translator's jurisdiction profile.
Cross-check the Insurer FEIN (DN0074) and Claim Administrator FEIN (DN0187) held in the translator against the values on the signed agreement — a single-digit difference rejects every transaction.
Confirm the same FEINs and NAIC codes are the ones the Policy Administration Analyst reports on proof of coverage, so claim and policy records match at the state.
Lock the identifier fields so they can only be changed through a reviewed change ticket.
checklist.done: translator identifiers match the signed agreement and the proof-of-coverage identifiers character for character.

checklist.step: Stand up and secure the transmission channel
actions: Configure the channel the state accepts — SFTP to the division's mailbox, AS2, or upload to the state's contracted EDI clearinghouse — with the endpoint host, port and directory paths from the state guide.
Store keys and passwords in the credential vault, never in the translator config, and record the rotation date.
Ask the Infrastructure / Network Engineer to allow-list the state endpoint on both directions and to confirm the inbound acknowledgment mailbox is polled on a schedule.
Prove a round trip by sending a zero-record structural file and confirming the acknowledgment mailbox receives the response.
checklist.done: an outbound and inbound round trip completes over the state-accepted channel with credentials held in the vault.

checklist.step: Complete the state's structure and content certification tests
actions: Work the state's test script in order: structural/syntax test file, then the content test scenarios the state prescribes (original FROI, change, cancel, denial, initial payment, suspension, final).
Send each test batch to the state's test mailbox and record the acknowledgment code returned per test transaction.
Correct any DN error the state returns, re-run the failing scenario, and keep every cycle's file and acknowledgment as the test record.
Do not request production status until every prescribed scenario returns TA.
checklist.done: every prescribed test scenario returns an accepted acknowledgment and the full test cycle is retained.

checklist.step: Obtain and file the state's production approval
actions: Request production status from the state EDI coordinator, citing the completed test scenarios and dates.
File the state's written approval or production-status notice under WC-EDI/<state>/registration and record the production start date.
Switch the jurisdiction profile from test to production only after the written approval is on file — never on a verbal go-ahead.
Notify the Claims Director / Manager of the production start date so filings are released from that date, not before.
checklist.done: written state production approval is on file and the jurisdiction profile flips to production on the approved date.

checklist.step: Load the jurisdiction element requirement table into the edit tables
actions: Take the state's Element Requirement Table from its implementation guide and load, per MTC, which DN elements are M (mandatory), MC (mandatory conditional), and the conditions that make MC apply.
Load the state's valid MTC list and its event table so an MTC the state does not accept cannot be released at all.
Load the state's error message and DN error-number table so acknowledgments can be translated automatically for the Claims Operations desk.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Analyst read the loaded table back against the published guide page by page and sign the comparison.
checklist.done: element, MTC and error tables for the jurisdiction match the published implementation guide with a signed page-by-page comparison.

checklist.step: Version-control the configuration and release it through change control
actions: Hold all jurisdiction profiles and edit tables as versioned files in the repository — no direct edits in the production translator console.
Raise a change ticket per release naming the jurisdiction, the state notice driving the change, the table version and the state's implementation date.
Require the Regulatory Reporting Manager's approval on the ticket before the pipeline promotes to production.
Record the deployed version number against the jurisdiction so any transaction can be tied to the table version that validated it.
checklist.done: every configuration change is a versioned, approved release with the deployed version recorded against the jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Subscribe to and triage IAIABC and state EDI change notices
actions: Subscribe the shared WC EDI mailbox to IAIABC release notices and to every state WC division's EDI bulletin distribution list.
Triage each notice within two business days: record the jurisdiction, the elements or MTCs affected, and the state's implementation date.
Raise a change ticket for anything requiring a table or mapping change and set the 90/60/30-day reminders against the implementation date.
Close notices requiring no action with a written 'no impact' rationale, not silently.
checklist.done: every notice is triaged within two business days into either a dated change ticket or a written no-impact rationale.

checklist.step: Regression-test edit table changes before release
actions: Run the standing regression pack — a fixed set of FROI 00, FROI 04, SROI IP, SROI SA and SROI FN scenarios per jurisdiction — against the new table version.
Confirm previously valid transactions still validate and that the newly required elements now fail when absent.
Re-run the state's own test scenarios in the state test mailbox where the state requires re-certification for the release.
Attach the regression results to the change ticket; a red pack blocks the promotion.
checklist.done: the regression pack and any state re-certification pass on the new table version and are attached to the change ticket.

checklist.step: Maintain registration currency, contacts and credentials
actions: Run the quarterly currency check: registration expiry or renewal date per state, named contact still employed, credential rotation date, endpoint certificate expiry.
File an updated trading-partner profile with the state whenever a contact, FEIN, sender ID, address or claim administrator changes — before the change takes effect operationally.
Rotate SFTP keys and AS2 certificates on schedule and confirm a successful round trip after each rotation.
Record each currency check with its date and the states touched.
checklist.done: every state registration is current with live contacts, unexpired credentials and a dated quarterly currency check.

checklist.step: Oversee the EDI vendor or clearinghouse used in the states that require one
actions: List the states where transmissions route through a contracted clearinghouse rather than direct to the division, and hold the current contract for each.
Confirm the contract names the carrier as the responsible party for filing accuracy and requires the vendor to pass acknowledgments through unaltered within one business day.
Review the vendor's monthly transmission and acknowledgment statistics against the internal transmission log and challenge any gap.
Confirm the vendor's own state registration is current before each renewal is signed.
checklist.done: each clearinghouse state has a current contract, pass-through acknowledgment terms, and a reconciled monthly vendor statistic.

checklist.step: Prove the EDI channel survives an outage
actions: Document the fallback route per state (secondary endpoint, manual upload to the state portal, or paper first report where the state still permits one).
Run a tabletop each half-year on a 72-hour translator outage and record how the statutory clocks would still be met.
Set the incident priority for an EDI transmission failure to reflect the statutory clock — an outage during a filing window is a P1, not a P3.
Record the tested recovery time against the shortest statutory clock in the book (Alaska and California business-day clocks).
checklist.done: a tested fallback exists per state and the recovery time is shorter than the tightest statutory filing clock.

checklist.step: Reconcile the configuration against the state's published trading-partner status
actions: Each quarter, ask each state EDI coordinator (or check the state's published trading-partner list where one exists) to confirm the registered sender ID, claim administrator FEIN and production status held on their side.
Compare their answer to the translator jurisdiction profile field by field.
Correct any difference by filing an updated profile with the state and by raising a change ticket internally on the same day.
File the state's confirmation as the quarter's evidence of registration currency.
checklist.done: each state's own record of the trading partner is confirmed in writing and agrees with the translator profile.

checklist.step: Retain the registration and configuration evidence
actions: Archive per state: signed trading-partner agreement and profile, certification test files and acknowledgments, production approval letter, and each dated edit-table version with its release note and approver.
Apply a 7-year-from-supersession retention label so a superseded configuration is still producible for a look-back review.
Index by state, sender ID, table version and effective date range so any historic transaction can be tied to the configuration that validated it.
Confirm quarterly that the index resolves at least one archived version per active jurisdiction.
checklist.done: registration and configuration evidence is archived, retention-labelled and indexed so any transaction maps to its governing table version.

testing.step: Build the population of jurisdictions and configuration changes
actions: List all 30 jurisdiction profiles active at the test date from the translator configuration export.
Extract every trading-partner and edit-table change promoted to production in the quarter from the release log, with version, promoter, approver and deploy timestamp.
Add any change applied directly in the production console — these are exceptions by definition and must still enter the population.
Sign the population as complete with the export queries and run date.
testing.done: the population lists every active jurisdiction and every production configuration change in the quarter, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the jurisdiction list to the in-force policy footprint
actions: Extract the WC in-force policy list by coverage state at the test date and by state with any claim opened in the quarter.
Compare that state list to the registered jurisdiction list and identify any state with exposure but no registration.
Confirm each registered jurisdiction shows production status rather than test status in the translator profile.
Treat any writing state with no production registration as an automatic fail, whatever the claim volume.
testing.done: every state with in-force WC exposure or claim activity has a production-status registration, or is raised as a fail.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of configuration changes
actions: Take 100% of trading-partner registration changes and 100% of changes driven by a state implementation date in the quarter.
Take 15 edit-table changes at random with a recorded seed from the remaining promotions.
Add every direct production-console change identified in the population, regardless of count.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all registration changes, all deadline-driven changes and any console-applied change.

testing.step: Re-perform the edit table against the state's published guide
actions: For Alabama and two further sampled states, download the current Claims EDI implementation guide and take the Element Requirement Table for FROI 00 and SROI IP.
Compare, element by element, the M/MC flags in the deployed edit table to the guide and note every disagreement with its DN number.
Check the valid MTC list in the table against the state's event table — an MTC the state does not accept but the table permits is a live rejection risk.
Screenshot the guide pages relied on into the workpaper with their publication date.
testing.done: the deployed element and MTC tables are compared element by element to the current published guide, with differences listed by DN number.

testing.step: Verify registrations and certification evidence per state
actions: For each sampled state, open the signed trading-partner agreement and confirm it is signed by both parties and not superseded.
Confirm a written state production approval or acknowledgment exists and pre-dates the first production transmission for that state.
Compare the Insurer FEIN, Claim Administrator FEIN and sender ID on the agreement to the values in the deployed jurisdiction profile.
List any state relying on a verbal or undated approval as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled state has a countersigned agreement, a dated production approval pre-dating first transmission, and matching identifiers.

testing.step: Test change control on the sampled promotions
actions: For each sampled change, open the change ticket and confirm it names the state notice or IAIABC release that drove it.
Confirm the Regulatory Reporting Manager's approval is recorded and pre-dates the production deploy timestamp.
Confirm the regression pack results are attached and green, and that promoter and approver are different people.
Treat any deploy with approval timestamped after the deploy as an exception, whatever the outcome.
testing.done: every sampled promotion has a dated pre-deploy approval by a second person with green regression evidence attached.

testing.step: Recompute renewal, expiry and implementation-date maths
actions: For each of the 30 registrations, recompute days remaining to renewal or credential/certificate expiry from the state's stated cycle and today's date.
For each state implementation date published in the quarter, compare the deployed table's production date to the state's mandated date and compute days early or late.
Confirm the 90/60/30-day reminders were actually raised for each implementation date rather than assumed.
List any registration inside 60 days of expiry with no renewal ticket open.
testing.done: renewal and implementation-date maths is independently recomputed with every late deploy and unrenewed registration listed.

testing.step: Test that transmissions could not run under a lapsed or test-mode profile
actions: Sample 10 production transmissions from the quarter and tie each to the jurisdiction profile version and table version in force at its transmission timestamp.
Confirm that profile was in production status with a current registration on that date.
Attempt, in the test environment, to release a transaction under a disabled jurisdiction profile and confirm the translator blocks it.
Confirm identifier fields are locked against edit outside a change ticket by checking the console permission set.
testing.done: every sampled transmission maps to a current production profile, and the control blocking lapsed-profile transmission is demonstrated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the jurisdiction, the configuration item, the table or profile version, and the exposure window in days.
Assign a root cause (notice not triaged, approval bypassed, console edit, credential lapse, vendor change unnotified) and a named owner.
For any state found transmitting under a lapsed registration, quantify the transactions sent in the exposure window and route the position to Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, exposure window and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare results to the zero-tolerance thresholds: no unregistered active jurisdiction, no table behind a state implementation date, no unapproved promotion.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references for each exception.
Have the independent reviewer, who holds no write access to the translator configuration, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the IT change board, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception list and dual reporting to the compliance and change forums exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns proof-of-coverage reporting for every WC policy event across the 30 jurisdictions; Policy Administration builds and releases the POC records, with Regulatory Reporting owning the state relationship (rep jurisdiction: Alaska Workers' Compensation Division)

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Title 21 of the Alaska Statutes together with the Alaska Workers' Compensation Division's proof-of-coverage filing requirements and the IAIABC POC/WCPOLS record layout; Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27) and the Arkansas Insurance Code re-read at each state's POC release change

In-scope processes.value: WC policy issuance, renewal, cancellation, non-renewal, reinstatement and endorsements that change named insured, FEIN, coverage state or coverage dates — every one of which is a POC-reportable event in the 30 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: PolicyCenter policy-event triggers feeding the WCPOLS-format POC extract through the EDI translator; POC acknowledgments written back to the policy record

Compliance procedure documented.value: WC Proof of Coverage Reporting Procedure — event-to-record-type mapping (new, renewal, cancellation, reinstatement, endorsement), required WCPOLS elements, the 30-day filing clock, and rejection handling

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Head of Compliance; re-approved on each state POC release change and whenever a state moves POC collection between the division and NCCI

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per policy event — POC filed within 30 days of the policy effective date for new and renewal business, and cancellations reported within the state's cancellation-notice period (Alaska cancellation notice runs to the division as well as the insured); each state's clock held in the POC jurisdiction table

Deadline reminders configured.value: PolicyCenter POC queue alerts at day 10 and day 20 of the 30-day clock, plus a same-day alert on any cancellation or reinstatement transaction, worked by the policy operations desk each morning

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: POC record images, the state or NCCI acknowledgment with its accept/reject code and error list, and the resubmission chain, retained on the policy record for the policy term plus 7 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any policy event with no POC transmission inside its clock, or a rejected POC left uncorrected, is raised with policy number, state, event type, day count and the coverage-verification risk it creates for the employer

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late POC remediation and any correction to a state coverage database that showed an employer as uninsured

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All WC policy transactions (new, renewal, cancellation, non-renewal, reinstatement, POC-relevant endorsement) with a transaction effective date in the quarter, across the 30 jurisdictions, from the policy transaction register

Pass/fail thresholds.value: ≥99.5% of POC events filed inside the state clock; any policy in force with no accepted POC record at the state, and any cancellation not reported, is an automatic fail — an employer showing uninsured on a state lookup is a reportable breach

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per policy event; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's transactions, with a monthly automated in-force-versus-state-coverage reconciliation feeding it

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Policy Administration and must not have keyed or released any sampled POC record

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly WC POC workpaper (transaction extract, in-force-to-state reconciliation, sample re-performance, 30-day recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under WC-POC/<yyyy-Qn>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-policy POC history showing record type, transmission date, acknowledgment code and the coverage dates on file at the state, producible for an Alaska Workers' Compensation Division coverage audit within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager answers state coverage-verification enquiries and NCCI POC queries; Regulatory Counsel clears any position on a period where a covered employer appeared uninsured on the state database

checklist.step: Identify the POC-reportable policy events for the day
actions: Open the daily policy transaction register filtered to Line = Workers' Compensation and Status = Bound/Issued.
Select the reportable event types: new business, renewal, cancellation, non-renewal, reinstatement, and endorsements changing named insured, FEIN, coverage state or coverage dates.
Exclude non-reportable endorsements (premium-only, billing plan, mailing address) and record the exclusion reason on the register.
Push the reportable set into the POC queue with the transaction effective date carried through.
checklist.done: the day's reportable events sit in the POC queue with effective dates, and every excluded transaction carries a written reason.

checklist.step: Map each event to its POC record type and state clock
actions: Open the POC jurisdiction table and read the state's row: collecting body (state division direct or NCCI on the state's behalf), accepted POC release, and filing clock.
Map the transaction to the WCPOLS record type: new/renewal policy record, cancellation record, reinstatement record, or policy change record.
For Alaska, confirm the record routes to the Alaska Workers' Compensation Division and apply the 30-day-from-effective-date clock.
Stamp the record type, collecting body and computed due date onto the POC queue item.
checklist.done: each queue item shows record type, collecting body and a computed due date derived from the transaction effective date.

checklist.step: Assemble the required coverage elements from the policy record
actions: Populate the carrier fields: insurer name, Insurer FEIN and NAIC company code of the writing company that actually issued the policy — not the group parent.
Populate the insured fields: legal entity name, all trading/DBA names, FEIN, and the physical address of every covered location in the state.
Populate policy number, effective date, expiration date, and the 3A coverage states listed on the information page.
Populate the governing class codes and any state-specific endorsements affecting coverage, taking them from the issued information page rather than the quote.
checklist.done: the POC record carries writing-company identifiers, insured legal name/DBA/FEIN, locations, coverage dates and 3A states from the issued information page.

checklist.step: Validate the insured FEIN and legal name against source
actions: Compare the FEIN on the POC record to the FEIN captured on the signed application and on the premium audit record.
Reject a nine-digit FEIN that is all zeroes, a repeated digit, or the producer's own FEIN — these pass format edits and fail state matching.
Where the insured has multiple FEINs across entities, confirm the FEIN reported is the one employing the workers in that coverage state.
Correct at source in the customer master so the next transaction inherits the fix.
checklist.done: every POC record's FEIN and legal name are traced to the application or audit record and corrected at master-data source where wrong.

checklist.step: Run POC edit validation and clear errors before release
actions: Run the POC validation job and read the returned element errors against the state's POC element requirement table.
Check date logic: expiration after effective, cancellation date within the policy term, reinstatement date after the cancellation date.
Check the coverage state on the record is one the policy's 3A item actually lists — a mismatch creates a coverage record the state cannot match to an employer.
Fix in the policy record, re-run validation to zero errors, and mark 'ready to release'.
checklist.done: the POC record passes validation with zero element errors and consistent date and coverage-state logic.

checklist.step: Transmit the new and renewal POC records inside the 30-day clock
actions: Release the day's POC batch to the state division or to NCCI on the state's behalf over the registered trading-partner channel.
Record transmission date, batch control number and record count against each policy.
Compare transmission date to the 30-day due date and mark each record on-time or late immediately.
Confirm the batch record count released equals the queue count selected — a short batch is a silent non-filing.
checklist.done: the POC batch is transmitted with a recorded control number, record counts reconciled, and each record flagged on-time or late.

checklist.step: Report cancellations and non-renewals on their own clock
actions: On issuing a cancellation or non-renewal notice, take the cancellation effective date, the reason code (non-payment, insured request, underwriting) and the notice mail date.
Build the POC cancellation record with the cancellation effective date, not the notice date, and release it inside the state's cancellation-reporting period.
Confirm the notice actually mailed to the insured on the recorded date by checking the print-and-mail vendor confirmation.
Where the cancellation is later rescinded, release a reinstatement record the same day so the state does not carry the employer as uninsured.
checklist.done: every cancellation, non-renewal and reinstatement has a matching POC record filed on its own clock with dates tied to the issued notice.

checklist.step: Report POC-relevant endorsements as policy change records
actions: Screen each endorsement for POC relevance: named insured change, FEIN change, added or deleted 3A coverage state, added covered location, coverage date change.
Build a policy change record carrying both the prior and the new value of the changed element so the state can match to the existing coverage record.
Add a new state to the POC feed on the endorsement effective date — a state added mid-term with no POC record leaves employees uncovered on the state database.
Note the endorsement number and effective date on the POC record for traceability.
checklist.done: every POC-relevant endorsement produces a change record showing prior and new values and referencing the endorsement number.

checklist.step: Capture the POC acknowledgment and write it back to the policy
actions: Poll the POC inbound mailbox daily and load acknowledgments against the outbound batch control numbers.
Read the per-record disposition (accepted, accepted with errors, rejected) and the returned error codes.
Write the accepted status, the acknowledgment date and any state-assigned coverage identifier back onto the policy record.
Reconcile records released to records acknowledged and list any unmatched record for follow-up within two business days.
checklist.done: every released POC record has a matched acknowledgment written back to the policy, or sits on a dated follow-up list.

checklist.step: Correct and resubmit rejected POC records
actions: Open each rejected record, translate the state's error code, and identify the failing element — most rejections are FEIN mismatch, unknown carrier code or an out-of-term date.
Correct the underlying policy or customer-master data, then rebuild and re-release the record rather than editing the outbound file.
Where the original 30-day clock has already run, log the filing as late and record the days the employer sat unmatched at the state.
Escalate any error appearing on more than five policies in a week to the Business Systems Analyst as a mapping defect.
checklist.done: every rejected POC record is corrected at source, re-released and accepted, with recurring errors escalated as defects.

checklist.step: Reconcile the in-force book to the state coverage database monthly
actions: Extract the WC in-force policy list by coverage state as at month end from policy administration.
Pull the coverage records the state or NCCI holds for the carrier's FEIN and compare policy number, effective and expiration dates and insured FEIN.
Investigate three break types separately: in force with us but absent at the state, present at the state but cancelled with us, and date or FEIN mismatches.
Clear each break with a corrective POC record and record the days the break was open.
checklist.done: the monthly in-force-to-state reconciliation is complete, with every break cleared by a corrective record and its open days recorded.

checklist.step: Answer state and employer coverage-verification enquiries
actions: Take coverage-verification enquiries from the state division, an employer, or a claim adjuster who cannot match a claim to a policy at the state.
Pull the policy's POC transmission history and the state's held coverage record and identify which side is wrong.
Answer the enquirer within two business days with the policy number, coverage dates and the corrective POC record reference where one was needed.
Log every enquiry — a rising count is the leading indicator of a POC feed defect.
checklist.done: every coverage-verification enquiry is answered within two business days with a documented cause and any corrective record referenced.

checklist.step: Report POC performance to the operating forum monthly
actions: Publish the monthly POC pack: records released, on-time percentage against the 30-day clock, rejection rate by error code, open reconciliation breaks by state and age.
Call out any state where on-time performance fell below 99.5% and name the owner and the fix.
Review the oldest open break in every state and set a closure date in the meeting.
Export the pack with its date as the evidence the review happened.
checklist.done: a dated monthly pack is published and reviewed, with named owners and closure dates against every sub-threshold state and aged break.

checklist.step: Log late or missed POC filings and assess the employer impact
actions: Raise an issue per late or missed POC event with policy number, state, event type, effective date, due date and days over.
Assign a root cause (event not flagged, FEIN rejection, batch short-shipped, endorsement not screened, state release change) and an owner.
For any period where an insured employer showed as uninsured on the state database, record the exposure days and route the notification position through Regulatory Counsel.
Carry each open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
checklist.done: every late or missed POC event has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a recorded employer-exposure assessment.

checklist.step: Retain the POC records and acknowledgments
actions: Archive the POC record image, the acknowledgment with its disposition and error codes, and the correction chain against the policy record.
Apply the 'policy term + 7 years' retention label so records survive policy expiry and audit look-backs.
Index by state, policy number, insured FEIN and transmission date so a state coverage query can be answered from any of them.
Spot-check ten archived policies a quarter to confirm images open and the index returns them.
checklist.done: POC records and acknowledgments are archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by policy number and insured FEIN.

testing.step: Build the population of POC-reportable policy transactions
actions: Extract every WC policy transaction with an effective date in the quarter across the 30 jurisdictions: new, renewal, cancellation, non-renewal, reinstatement and endorsement.
Classify each as POC-reportable or not using the state's own event rules, independently of the flag the business set.
Reconcile transaction counts to the policy administration transaction register and the written-premium ledger for the quarter.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction query and run date.
testing.done: the population covers every WC policy transaction in the quarter, independently classified and reconciled to the transaction register.

testing.step: Reconcile the in-force book to the state coverage records
actions: Take the WC in-force listing at quarter end by coverage state and match it to the coverage records held by each state division or by NCCI for the carrier FEIN.
List policies in force with us but absent at the state — each is an employer the state would report as uninsured.
List coverage records live at the state for policies we cancelled, and any effective/expiration date or FEIN mismatch.
Confirm the operational monthly reconciliation identified the same breaks; breaks it missed are control exceptions in their own right.
testing.done: the independent in-force-to-state match is complete and every break is either already on the operational log or raised as a missed-detection exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Alaska transactions and 100% of cancellations and reinstatements in the quarter.
Take 30 further transactions at random with a recorded seed, stratified so new business, renewal and POC-relevant endorsement each appear at least eight times.
Add every policy on the in-force-to-state break list regardless of count.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers Alaska and all cancellations in full, and includes every reconciliation break.

testing.step: Re-perform the record type and reportability call
actions: For each sampled transaction, read the state's POC requirements and reach your own conclusion on reportability and record type before opening the POC history.
Compare to what was actually filed; an endorsement adding a coverage state that was treated as non-reportable is an exception.
Confirm the collecting body used (state division direct versus NCCI) matches what the state currently mandates.
Record your conclusion, the filed record type and any difference on the workpaper line.
testing.done: each sampled transaction carries an independent reportability and record-type conclusion with differences logged.

testing.step: Trace POC content back to the issued policy documents
actions: Open the issued information page for each sampled policy and compare insured legal name, DBA, FEIN, policy number and effective/expiration dates to the transmitted POC record.
Compare the 3A coverage states on the information page to the coverage states on the POC record and list any state present on one and not the other.
For cancellations, compare the POC cancellation date to the cancellation notice and the print-and-mail confirmation date.
Treat a FEIN that is the producer's, the parent's, or a placeholder as a content failure rather than a formatting note.
testing.done: every sampled POC record's insured, policy and coverage-state content is traced to the issued information page or cancellation notice.

testing.step: Trace each sampled record to an accepted acknowledgment
actions: Search the POC history by batch control number and confirm an acknowledgment exists for each sampled record.
Read the final disposition and confirm that any rejection was followed by a corrected re-release that was accepted.
Confirm the accepted status and any state-assigned coverage identifier were written back onto the policy record.
Capture the acknowledgment detail into the workpaper as trace evidence.
testing.done: every sampled POC record traces to a final accepted acknowledgment recorded against the policy.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day clock and the cancellation-reporting clock
actions: Recompute elapsed days = transmission date − policy effective date for each sampled new and renewal record and compare to the state's 30-day requirement (Alaska rep).
Recompute cancellation reporting days = transmission date − cancellation effective date and compare to the state's cancellation-reporting period.
Confirm calendar-day versus business-day treatment per state; the wrong convention understates lateness across the whole population.
Recompute the on-time percentage from the sample and reconcile it to the monthly POC pack figure.
testing.done: clocks are independently recomputed per state convention and the recomputed on-time rate is reconciled to the published monthly pack.

testing.step: Test rejection closure and the correction-at-source rule
actions: Extract every rejected POC record in the quarter and age each from rejection to accepted re-release.
Confirm the correction was made in the policy or customer master by re-reading the element on the policy record, not just in the resent file.
Confirm no rejected record was closed without an accepted acknowledgment.
Test that a re-corrected FEIN persisted into the next transaction on the same policy.
testing.done: every rejection is shown corrected at source, re-accepted, and the correction is proven to persist to the next transaction.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and employer exposure
actions: Raise an issue per exception with policy number, state, event type, effective date, due date, days over and acknowledgment status.
Assign a root cause (event not flagged, endorsement not screened, FEIN rejection, short batch, state release change) and a named owner.
For every period an insured employer was absent from the state coverage database, record the exposure days and any downstream effect on a claim that could not be matched to a policy.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a quantified employer-exposure period.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the POC on-time rate and compare to the 99.5% threshold and the zero-unfiled-in-force rule.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references behind each exception.
Have the independent reviewer, who keyed or released none of the sampled records, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any employer-uninsured exposure to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the on-time rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.
