Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs daily; the control is evidenced daily and independently tested monthly over the full month's transmission and acknowledgment logs

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Claims Operations and must not have corrected or re-released any sampled rejected transaction

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly WC EDI rejection workpaper (transmission-to-ack reconciliation, aging analysis, DN error root-cause table, sample re-performance) in the compliance evidence repository under WC-EDI-REJECT/<yyyy-mm>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-claim rejection and correction chain showing the original transmission, the acknowledgment with DN errors, the correction made and the accepted re-transmission date, producible for an Alabama WC Division EDI review within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager raises unresolved or disputed rejections with the state EDI coordinator; Regulatory Counsel clears any position where a statutory clock expired because a transaction sat rejected

checklist.step: Pull and load the day's acknowledgment files
actions: Poll each jurisdiction's inbound mailbox before 08:00 local and download the acknowledgment files awaiting collection.
Load each file into the translator against its outbound batch and interchange control numbers.
Confirm the load count equals the file's record count; a partial load is escalated to the Integration Engineer before the desk starts work.
Publish the loaded acknowledgment set into the EDI desk's work queue with a load timestamp.
checklist.done: all jurisdiction mailboxes are polled and loaded before the desk opens, with record counts reconciled to the files received.

checklist.step: Reconcile transmissions released against acknowledgments received
actions: Run the daily reconciliation report: transactions released in the prior 24 hours by jurisdiction versus acknowledgments matched.
List unmatched outbound transactions with their transmission date and age in business days.
Verify totals by jurisdiction rather than in aggregate — one silent mailbox hides behind a healthy group total.
Save the dated reconciliation report as the day's evidence that the control operated.
checklist.done: a dated per-jurisdiction reconciliation report exists showing matched, unmatched and aged transmissions.

checklist.step: Classify every acknowledgment by disposition code
actions: Split the day's acknowledgments into TA (accepted), TE (accepted with errors) and TR (rejected) buckets.
For TA, confirm the jurisdiction claim number returned has been written back to the claim record — later SROIs reject without it.
For TE, record which DN elements the state accepted under protest and the correction it expects on the next transaction.
For TR, mark the claim as having no report on file at the state and re-arm the original statutory clock on the filing task.
checklist.done: every acknowledgment is classified, jurisdiction claim numbers are written back, and every TR claim shows its statutory clock still running.

checklist.step: Triage rejections by DN error number
actions: Translate each returned DN error number and error message code against the jurisdiction's published error table.

Bucket each error: claim data error (wrong date, missing wage), identity error (FEIN, policy number, jurisdiction claim number), sequencing error (SROI sent before an accepted FROI), or format/mapping error.
Route claim data and identity errors to the owning adjuster; route sequencing and format errors to the Business Systems Analyst.
Set a correction target of 2 business days on every item at triage.
checklist.done: every rejected transaction carries a translated error, an assigned bucket, a named owner and a 2-business-day correction target.

checklist.step: Correct claim data errors at source in the claims system
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Open the claim, go to the element the DN error names, and correct it against the source document — employer first report, wage statement, medical report or payment transaction.
Never patch the outbound file: a file-only fix reappears on the next transaction for the same claim.
Where the source document itself is wrong or missing, request a corrected document from the employer or provider and note the request date on the claim.
Record the correction and its source on the claim note so the auditor can retrace it.
checklist.done: the failing element is corrected in the claim record against a named source document, with the correction noted.

checklist.step: Fix identity and policy-match rejections with Policy Administration
actions: For 'policy not found' or 'employer not on file' rejections, compare the policy number, insurer FEIN and insured FEIN on the transaction to the filed proof-of-coverage record.
Ask the Policy Administration Analyst to confirm whether the POC record for that policy and coverage state was accepted at the state, and to file a corrective POC where it was not.
Hold the claim transaction until the POC is accepted, then re-release — resending against a missing coverage record just rejects again.
Record the linked POC correction reference on the claim's EDI history.
checklist.done: identity rejections are resolved by proving an accepted POC record exists, with the corrective POC reference recorded on the claim.

checklist.step: Re-release the corrected transaction with the right MTC
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: For a TR item, re-send the original MTC — the state holds no report, so an MTC 02 change would itself reject.
For a TE item, send an MTC 02 change transaction carrying the corrected element.
Re-run pre-submission validation to zero errors before release and record the new batch control number against the claim.
Compare the re-release date to the original statutory due date and flag the filing late where the clock has already run.
checklist.done: the corrected transaction is re-released with the correct MTC, validated clean, and marked on-time or late against the original clock.

checklist.step: Chase transmissions with no acknowledgment
actions: Work the unacknowledged list daily and age each item from its transmission date.

At 5 business days, confirm with the Integration Engineer that the file left the gateway and reached the state endpoint, then email the state EDI coordinator quoting the batch control number, sender ID and transmission timestamp.
Where the state confirms non-receipt, re-transmit the batch the same day and log the original as a failed transmission, not as a filed report.
Record every chase, the date and the state's answer against the claim.
checklist.done: no transmission sits unacknowledged past 5 business days without a logged chase and a documented state answer.

checklist.step: Escalate rejections that are aging past target
actions: Read the reject aging tile each morning: items at 2, 5 and 10 business days by jurisdiction and error bucket.
Reassign anything at 5 days to a named senior adjuster with a same-day clearance instruction.
Escalate anything at 10 days to the Head of Compliance with the claim number, the DN error and the statutory clock status.
Record the daily review as a dated dashboard export.
checklist.done: the aging tile is reviewed and exported daily, with 5-day items reassigned and 10-day items escalated to Compliance.

checklist.step: Run root-cause analysis on the week's error pattern
actions: Build the weekly Pareto of DN error numbers by jurisdiction and count, and take the top five.
For each, decide whether the cause is a mapping defect, a stale edit table, a claims data-capture gap or an adjuster training gap.
Raise a change ticket for mapping and edit-table causes and hand data-capture and training causes to the Claims Quality Assurance / Training Manager.
Track each top-five error's count into the following week to prove the fix worked.
checklist.done: the weekly top-five DN errors each have a named cause, a raised ticket or training action, and a tracked count in the following week.

checklist.step: Feed edit-table and mapping defects into change control
actions: Convert each confirmed mapping or edit-table defect into a versioned configuration change with the jurisdiction and DN element named in the commit.
Add a regression scenario reproducing the rejection so the defect cannot return silently.
Route the change for the Regulatory Reporting Manager's approval before promotion, as required by the configuration procedure.
Report the deployed version back to the reject queue so open items can be re-released against the fixed table.
checklist.done: each confirmed defect is a versioned, approved, regression-covered change with its deployed version fed back to the reject queue.

checklist.step: Maintain the daily exception log
actions: Log each rejection open past its 2-day target and each unacknowledged transmission past 5 days with claim number, jurisdiction, DN error, age and statutory clock status.
Update the age and status on every open item daily rather than at month end.
Close an item only against an accepted acknowledgment reference — never on 'resent' alone.
Export the log daily so the aging population can be rebuilt for any past date.
checklist.done: the exception log is updated daily, closed only against accepted acknowledgments, and exported so any historic day can be rebuilt.

checklist.step: Report rejection performance to the claims governance forum monthly
actions: Publish the monthly pack: transmissions released, acknowledgment match rate, TE/TR rate by jurisdiction, clearance within 5 business days, and items aged past 10 days.
Name every jurisdiction below the 95% five-day clearance threshold with its owner and remediation date.
Present the count of claims where a statutory clock expired while a transaction sat rejected — this is the number that becomes a penalty.
Export the dated pack as evidence the review took place.
checklist.done: a dated monthly pack is reviewed showing match rate, clearance rate, aged items and clock-expiry counts with named owners.

checklist.step: Track state penalty notices arising from rejected filings
actions: Log each state penalty or non-compliance notice with the jurisdiction, claim number, cited statute and the amount assessed.
Pull the claim's rejection and correction chain and determine whether the filing was late because of the rejection or because of the original release.
Route the response through Regulatory Counsel before it is filed with the state, including any request for penalty mitigation based on the correction record.
Link the notice to the underlying root cause so recurrence is visible.
checklist.done: every penalty notice is logged, tied to a rejection chain and a root cause, and answered through Regulatory Counsel.

checklist.step: Retain the reconciliation, rejection and correction evidence
actions: Archive the daily reconciliation report, the acknowledgment files, the exception log export and the weekly Pareto for each month.
Archive the per-claim correction chain (original transmission, acknowledgment with DN errors, correction note, accepted re-transmission) against the claim file.
Apply the 'life of claim + 5 years' retention label to claim-level records and a 7-year label to the daily reconciliation reports.
Confirm quarterly that a chosen claim's full chain can be reassembled from the archive alone.
checklist.done: daily reconciliations and per-claim correction chains are archived, retention-labelled, and provably reassemblable from the archive.

testing.step: Build the population of transmissions and acknowledgments
actions: Extract every outbound FROI/SROI transmission in the test month from the translator log with jurisdiction, claim number, MTC, batch control number and timestamp.
Extract every inbound acknowledgment with its disposition code, DN error numbers and receipt timestamp.
Count both sides by jurisdiction and day so a silent mailbox or a missing day is visible before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with the extraction queries and run date.
testing.done: outbound and inbound populations are extracted, counted by jurisdiction and day, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the two populations independently of the daily report
actions: Match transmissions to acknowledgments on batch and interchange control number and list every unmatched transmission.
Compare your unmatched list to the operational daily reconciliation reports for the same days; anything you found that the daily report did not is a control-failure exception.
Confirm the daily reconciliation report exists and is dated for every business day in the month — a missing day means the control did not operate.
Reconcile the total transmission count to the claims system's EDI release log so transmissions dropped before the translator are exposed.
testing.done: an independent match is complete, missing daily reports are identified, and every detection gap in the operational report is raised.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of rejected transactions
actions: Take 100% of TR rejections in Alabama and 100% of any rejection aged past 10 business days in any jurisdiction.
Take 30 further TE/TR items at random with a recorded seed, stratified across the top five DN error numbers for the month.
Add every unmatched transmission from the reconciliation step.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers Alabama rejections and all 10-day-plus items in full, and spans the top five error codes.

testing.step: Re-perform the DN error interpretation
actions: For each sampled item, take the DN error number and message code and look it up in the jurisdiction's current published error table yourself.
Reach your own conclusion on which element failed and why, before reading the desk's triage note.
Compare to the assigned error bucket and owner; a claim data error routed to IT as a mapping defect, or vice versa, is an exception because it delays the real fix.
Screenshot the error-table page relied on into the workpaper with its publication date.
testing.done: each sampled rejection has an independent error interpretation captured against the published error table, with mis-triage logged.

testing.step: Verify the correction was made at source, not in the file
testing.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Open the claim record for each sampled item and read the element the DN error named as it now stands.
Trace the corrected value to the source document cited on the claim note — employer first report, wage statement, payment transaction or corrected POC record.
Confirm the corrected value also appears on the next transaction released for that claim, proving the fix persisted.
Treat a claim record still holding the wrong value while the state holds a corrected one as an exception in its own right.
testing.done: each sampled correction is proven in the claim record, traced to a source document, and shown to persist on the next transaction.

testing.step: Trace re-releases to an accepted acknowledgment
actions: For each sampled item, find the re-release, confirm the MTC used matches the rule (original MTC after TR, MTC 02 after TE), and read its acknowledgment.
Confirm the final disposition is accepted; an item closed on the tracker without an accepted acknowledgment is an exception.
Check the jurisdiction claim number returned was written back to the claim where the re-release was a FROI.
Capture the acknowledgment detail into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled rejection traces to an accepted re-release with the correct MTC and, for FROIs, a recorded jurisdiction claim number.

testing.step: Recompute clearance ages and the statutory clock impact
actions: Recompute clearance age in business days = accepted re-release date − acknowledgment date for every TE/TR item in the month.
Recompute the five-business-day clearance rate and compare it to the 95% threshold and to the figure in the monthly pack.
For each TR item, recompute whether the original statutory clock (Alabama FROI, Florida 14-day, California 10-business-day) had expired by the accepted re-release date.
List every claim where the clock expired while the transaction sat rejected — these are penalty exposures, not test findings.
testing.done: clearance ages and the five-day rate are independently recomputed and every clock-expiry-while-rejected case is listed.

testing.step: Test the unacknowledged-transmission chase process
actions: Take every transmission unmatched after 5 business days and look for a logged chase with a date and the state's answer.
Confirm gateway evidence exists showing the file reached the state endpoint, and that a re-transmission followed where the state confirmed non-receipt.
Confirm no unmatched transmission was quietly reclassified as filed without an acknowledgment.
Age the remaining open unmatched items at the test date and report the oldest by jurisdiction.
testing.done: every aged unacknowledged transmission has a documented chase, gateway evidence and either an acknowledgment or a re-transmission.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with claim number, jurisdiction, DN error number, acknowledgment date, clearance date, age and clock status.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (claim data capture, identity/POC mismatch, sequencing, mapping defect, stale edit table, desk backlog, mailbox outage) and a named owner.
Open a Regulatory Counsel review for every claim where the statutory clock expired while the transaction was rejected.
Carry every open exception into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and — where a clock expired — a counsel review reference.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare results to the thresholds: 100% acknowledgment match, ≥95% cleared within 5 business days, nothing open past 10 business days.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references behind each exception.
Have the independent reviewer, who corrected or re-released none of the sampled transactions, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and every clock-expiry exposure to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with match rate, clearance rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns unit-statistical reporting to NCCI and the independent bureaus across the 30 jurisdictions; Actuarial / Stat Reporting builds and files the unit reports, with Claims and Premium Audit supplying valued data (rep jurisdiction: California, where the WCIRB is the statistical agent)

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations with the WCIRB California Uniform Statistical Reporting Plan and Unit Statistical Reporting Guide; for NCCI states, the NCCI Statistical Plan for Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance and the current WCSTAT record layout, re-read at each plan amendment

In-scope processes.value: Policy expiry → unit report due-date calendar → 18-month first-report valuation and the 30/42/54/66-month subsequent valuations → exposure, premium and claim data assembly → WCSTAT/USR build → bureau submission → criticism and correction cycle, for every WC policy in the 30 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: The statistical reporting mart holding valued policy exposure and premium from policy administration and valued claim indemnity/medical from the claims system, feeding the WCSTAT/USR build and the bureau submission channel (NCCI Data Manager; WCIRB Connect for California)

Compliance procedure documented.value: WC Unit Statistical Reporting Procedure — due-date calendar derivation, valuation cut rules, exposure and premium reconciliation to the general ledger, claim valuation rules, correction report rules and criticism clearance

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Statutory Reporting Manager; re-approved on each NCCI Statistical Plan amendment, each WCIRB reporting-plan change and any change of statistical agent in a state

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per schedule — first unit report valued at 18 months after policy effective date and due at 20 months; subsequent reports valued at 30, 42, 54 and 66 months and due three months after each valuation date; corrections due within the bureau's correction window after a criticism is issued

Deadline reminders configured.value: Statistical calendar reminders at 60, 30 and 10 days before each policy's unit report due date, and a same-week alert on every criticism file received from NCCI or the WCIRB

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submitted WCSTAT/USR files, bureau receipt and acceptance confirmations, criticism files and correction reports, and the premium and loss reconciliations to the general ledger, retained 7 years from the last valuation reported on the policy

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any unit report filed after its due date, rejected and left uncorrected, or filed with premium or losses that do not reconcile to the ledger, is logged with policy number, state, report level, valuation date and days late

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or restated unit report and any correction that moves a reported experience modification

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every WC policy with a unit report due in the quarter (first report at 20 months and subsequent reports at 33/45/57/69 months from policy effective date) across the 30 jurisdictions, from the statistical due-date calendar

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of due unit reports filed by the bureau due date and accepted; premium reported must reconcile to the ledger within 0.5% per state and losses within 1%; any policy with no unit report on file, or an open criticism past the bureau's correction window, is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per report on the bureau schedule; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's due population, with 100% coverage of California WCIRB submissions and of any policy carrying an experience modification

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Actuarial / Stat Reporting and must not have built, submitted or corrected any sampled unit report

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly unit-statistical workpaper (due-date population, ledger reconciliations, sample re-performance of valuations, criticism ageing, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under WC-USR/<yyyy-Qn>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-policy unit report pack — submitted file, bureau acceptance, valuation-date evidence, premium and loss reconciliation and any correction report — producible for a WCIRB or NCCI data audit within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Statutory Reporting Manager answers NCCI and WCIRB data-quality contacts and hosts bureau data audits; the Chief Actuary approves any restatement and Regulatory Counsel clears any position affecting a policyholder's experience modification

checklist.step: Build the unit report due-date calendar from the policy master
actions: Extract every WC policy with its effective date, expiration date, writing company, coverage states and cancellation status.
Compute the first report valuation date at 18 months from policy effective date and the due date at 20 months.
Compute subsequent valuations at 30, 42, 54 and 66 months with each due date three months after its valuation date, and stop the schedule where the bureau's plan stops.
Split the calendar by statistical agent: NCCI states, California to the WCIRB, and the other independent bureaus, since each takes its own file.
Publish the calendar with 60/30/10-day reminders per report.
checklist.done: every WC policy has its full valuation and due-date schedule computed, split by statistical agent, with reminders armed.

checklist.step: Confirm the reporting plan and record layout in force per bureau
actions: Read the current NCCI Statistical Plan and WCSTAT record layout, and the WCIRB California Uniform Statistical Reporting Plan for California policies.
Record the plan version and effective date against each state row in the statistical jurisdiction table.
List every layout change since the last submission — new fields, revised injury type or claim status codes, changed exposure rules — and hand them to the ETL Developer.
Note the bureau's own edit package version so the internal validation mirrors what they will run.
checklist.done: the plan and layout version in force is recorded per bureau, with layout changes handed to development and the edit package version noted.

checklist.step: Freeze the exposure and premium data at the valuation date
actions: Take the final audited payroll by class code and state for the policy term, including any endorsement changes, from the completed premium audit.
Where a premium audit is still open at the valuation date, escalate to the Premium Audit supervisor — an estimated exposure on a unit report drives a wrong experience modification.
Capture the premium build: manual premium by class, experience modification applied, schedule rating, expense constant, terrorism and catastrophe charges, and standard premium.
Freeze the extract as at the valuation date and label it with the policy, report level and valuation date.
checklist.done: audited exposure by class code and the full premium build are frozen as at the valuation date with open audits escalated.

checklist.step: Freeze the claim data valued at the valuation date
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Extract per claim on the policy: incurred indemnity and incurred medical (paid plus case outstanding) valued exactly at the valuation date, with no later development bleeding in.
Capture claim status (open/closed), injury type code (fatal, permanent total, major/minor permanent partial, temporary, medical only), accident date and jurisdiction.
Capture recoveries — subrogation, second-injury fund, deductible reimbursement — under the bureau's rules on gross versus net reporting.
Reconcile the claim-level total to the reserving system's valued triangle for that policy year and state before releasing the extract.
checklist.done: claim indemnity, medical, status and injury type are frozen at the valuation date and tie to the valued reserving triangle.

checklist.step: Reconcile reported premium and losses to the general ledger
actions: Roll the unit-report premium by state and policy year and compare it to written premium in the ledger for the same state and year.
Roll the unit-report incurred losses and compare them to the loss and LAE balances behind the statutory Schedule P by state and accident year.
Investigate any state variance over 0.5% on premium or 1% on losses down to the policy causing it — do not net offsetting variances.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the submission pack.
checklist.done: premium and loss totals reconcile to the ledger within tolerance by state, with every out-of-tolerance state traced to a named policy.

checklist.step: Build the WCSTAT/USR file
actions: Run the unit report build for the due population, generating header, exposure, loss and total records per the bureau's record layout.
Populate the header with carrier code, policy number as reported on proof of coverage, policy effective date, report level and valuation date.
Map class codes, injury type codes and claim status codes to the current bureau code lists — an outdated code list is the most common rejection cause.
Write the build run id, input extract labels and record counts into the run log so the file can be rebuilt identically.
checklist.done: the file builds cleanly with a logged run id, reconciled record counts and current bureau code lists applied.

checklist.step: Run the bureau's edit package before submission
actions: Run the internal replica of the bureau edit package and read the returned edit codes by severity.
Clear every fatal edit and give a written explanation for each warning edit that will be submitted as-is.
Check the standing sense tests: losses on a class code with no exposure, an open claim with zero incurred, a closed indemnity claim with zero paid indemnity, exposure with no premium.
Re-run to a clean fatal list and attach the edit report to the submission pack.
checklist.done: the file passes the replica edit package with zero fatal edits and every retained warning explained in writing.

checklist.step: Submit the unit reports to each bureau on schedule
actions: Submit NCCI-state unit reports through NCCI's Data Manager submission channel under the carrier code, and California reports to the WCIRB through its data submission channel.
Submit each independent-bureau state (for example the New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Wisconsin bureaus) in its own required format and channel.
Record the submission date, file name, record count and bureau confirmation reference against each policy in the calendar.
Compare the submission date to the due date and mark each report on-time or late immediately.
checklist.done: every due unit report is submitted to the right bureau with a recorded confirmation reference and an on-time/late flag.

checklist.step: Confirm bureau acceptance and record the rejected units
actions: Retrieve the bureau's processing response and split units into accepted, accepted-with-criticism, and rejected.
For rejected units, read the rejection reason — usually policy not on file, duplicate report level, or a valuation date outside the permitted window.

Where the rejection is 'policy not on file', check with the Policy Administration Analyst whether the policy's proof-of-coverage or policy data was reported to the bureau at all, and correct that first.
Re-submit rejected units and confirm acceptance before the due date wherever the window still allows it.
checklist.done: every submitted unit is confirmed accepted, or its rejection reason is recorded with a dated re-submission.

checklist.step: Work the bureau criticism file inside the correction window
actions: Load the criticism file from NCCI or the WCIRB and list each criticism by policy, criticism code and the field questioned.
Investigate each against the frozen source extracts — audited payroll, claim valuation, class assignment — rather than against today's values.
Answer with either a correction report carrying the amended value or a written response defending the reported value with its evidence.
Track each criticism to closure inside the bureau's correction window and record the closure date.
checklist.done: every criticism is answered with a correction report or a documented defence and closed inside the bureau's correction window.

checklist.step: File correction reports when reported data later proves wrong
actions: Raise a correction report where a premium audit is reopened, a claim is reclassified (for example medical-only reclassified as indemnity), or a class code assignment changes after submission.
Report the correction against the same policy, report level and valuation date as the original — never as a new report level.
Assess whether the correction moves the policyholder's experience modification and, if so, notify the Underwriting Director / Manager so renewal pricing is corrected.
Record the correction, its driver and its modification impact on the policy's statistical history.
checklist.done: each correction is filed at the original report level and valuation date, with any experience-modification impact assessed and notified.

checklist.step: Monitor the bureau's data quality scoring
actions: Track the bureau's data quality measures per submission cycle: timeliness, criticism rate per 100 units, and rejected-unit rate by state.
Compare each cycle to the bureau's published performance standard and to the prior cycle.
Where a state falls below standard, run a root-cause pass on that state's criticisms and raise the fix as a build or source-data change.
Publish the scorecard to the statistical reporting forum each cycle with named owners against every below-standard state.
checklist.done: a per-cycle bureau data-quality scorecard is published with root causes and named owners for every below-standard state.

checklist.step: Reconcile unit-statistical data to the statutory and financial calls
actions: Compare aggregate unit-report premium and losses by state to the bureau financial call submissions for the same period.
Compare the same figures to the statutory Annual Statement state page and Schedule P for the state and accident year.
Investigate and document every difference above tolerance, distinguishing genuine definitional differences (net versus gross of deductible reimbursements) from errors.
Attach the three-way reconciliation to the quarter's statistical reporting pack.
checklist.done: unit-statistical, financial call and Annual Statement figures are reconciled three ways with every difference explained in writing.

checklist.step: Escalate late, missing or restated unit reports
actions: Raise an issue per unit report filed after its due date, rejected and unrecovered, or restated after acceptance, with policy, state, report level, valuation date and days late.
Assign a root cause (premium audit open, claim valuation not frozen, policy not on bureau file, code list stale, calendar not built) and an owner.
For any late filing that could attract a bureau penalty or affect an experience modification, route the position through the Chief Actuary and Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
checklist.done: every late, missing or restated report has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and an assessed modification impact.

checklist.step: Retain the submission pack for the full retention period
actions: Archive per policy and report level: the submitted WCSTAT/USR file, the bureau confirmation, the edit report, the ledger reconciliation, the criticism file and any correction report.
Apply the 7-year-from-last-valuation retention label so the record survives the full 66-month reporting cycle plus audit look-back.
Index by state, carrier code, policy number, report level and valuation date so a WCIRB or NCCI data audit request resolves directly.
Confirm each quarter that a chosen policy's full five-level history can be reassembled from the archive alone.
checklist.done: each policy's unit report pack is archived, retention-labelled and provably reassemblable by report level and valuation date.

testing.step: Build the population of unit reports due in the quarter
actions: Independently recompute the due population from the policy master: every WC policy whose 20-month first-report due date or 33/45/57/69-month subsequent due date falls in the quarter.
Reconcile your recomputed population to the operational statistical calendar and list every policy the calendar missed.
Include cancelled and short-term policies, which still carry unit reporting obligations, and policies written in run-off states.
Sign the population as complete with the recomputation logic and run date.
testing.done: an independently recomputed due population exists and every policy missing from the operational calendar is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the due population to the in-force and expired policy master
actions: Reconcile the policy count in the due population to the count of WC policies with the corresponding effective-date months in the policy master.
Confirm each policy's writing company carrier code and coverage state match what the bureau holds, using the bureau's policy data on file.
Identify any policy in the master with no unit report at any level — these are silent non-filers, the worst outcome in this obligation.
Explain every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the due population reconciles to the policy master by effective-date cohort and every never-reported policy is identified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of California WCIRB submissions in the quarter and 100% of policies carrying an experience modification.
Take 25 further policies at random with a recorded seed, stratified so first reports and each subsequent report level appear at least four times.
Add every policy identified as a silent non-filer or as missing from the operational calendar.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers California and all experience-rated policies in full, and spans every report level.

testing.step: Re-perform the valuation and due-date maths
actions: For each sampled policy, recompute valuation date = policy effective date + 18/30/42/54/66 months and due date = valuation date + 2 months for the first report and + 3 months for subsequent reports, per the bureau plan in force.
Compare the recomputed valuation date to the valuation date carried in the submitted file header — a report valued a month early understates losses across the whole file.
Compare the recomputed due date to the actual submission date and compute days early or late.
List every report submitted outside the bureau's permitted valuation window as an exception even if it was accepted.
testing.done: valuation and due dates are independently recomputed per policy and every off-window valuation or late submission is listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the premium reconciliation to the ledger
actions: For each sampled policy, trace reported audited payroll by class code back to the completed premium audit worksheet.
Recompute standard premium: manual premium by class times the experience modification, plus schedule rating and expense constant, and compare to the reported figure.
Roll the sampled state's reported premium and compare to written premium in the ledger for that state and policy year, applying the 0.5% tolerance.
Flag any policy reported on estimated rather than audited exposure — the modification derived from it is wrong.
testing.done: reported premium is traced to the audit worksheet, recomputed, and reconciled to the ledger within tolerance per state.

testing.step: Re-perform the claim valuation trace
testing.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: For each sampled policy, take five claims and re-value indemnity and medical (paid plus case outstanding) as at the report's valuation date using the claim's transaction history.
Compare to the incurred amounts on the submitted unit report and list every difference.
Re-perform the injury type and claim status coding from the claim file — a medical-only claim reported as indemnity distorts the experience modification directly.
Confirm subrogation and deductible recoveries were treated on the bureau's gross/net basis, not the internal management basis.
testing.done: sampled claim values, injury types and statuses are re-performed at the valuation date and every difference is listed.

testing.step: Verify bureau acceptance and criticism closure
actions: For each sampled report, open the bureau confirmation and confirm the unit was accepted, not merely submitted.
Pull the criticism file entries for that policy and confirm each was closed by a correction report or a documented defence inside the bureau's correction window.
Age any open criticism at the test date and report the oldest by state.
Confirm rejected units were re-submitted and accepted, and that a 'policy not on file' rejection was cured by correcting the bureau policy data first.
testing.done: each sampled report is confirmed accepted with every criticism closed in window, and open criticisms are aged and reported.

testing.step: Test correction reports and their downstream pricing effect
actions: Extract every correction report filed in the quarter and confirm each was filed at the original report level and valuation date rather than as a new level.
For corrections that moved reported premium or losses materially, confirm the experience-modification impact was assessed and that Underwriting was notified where a renewal was affected.
Confirm the Chief Actuary's sign-off exists on every restatement.
List any correction discovered by the bureau rather than internally — that is a detection-control failure, not just a data error.
testing.done: every correction is filed at the correct level with a signed restatement approval and a documented modification impact assessment.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with policy number, state, bureau, report level, valuation date, due date, submission date and days late.
Assign a root cause (calendar gap, premium audit open at valuation, unfrozen claim extract, stale code list, policy not on bureau file, criticism unworked) and a named owner.
Quantify the effect on the policyholder's experience modification for every data exception and flag those needing a modification revision request to the bureau.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a quantified experience-modification impact.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare results to the thresholds: 100% of due reports filed and accepted by the due date, premium within 0.5% and losses within 1% of the ledger by state, no open criticism past window.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references behind each exception.
Have the independent reviewer, who built or submitted none of the sampled reports, sign the workpaper.
Report the result, any never-reported policies and any modification impacts to the Compliance Committee and the Chief Actuary, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with reconciliation results, a stated conclusion and dual reporting to the committee and Chief Actuary exists in the repository.
